text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- WORLD BANK TO FINANCE LAND PURCHASES BY PRODUCERS

The World Bank's board of directors Tuesday approved a $90 million loan for a $150-million program called "Agrarian Reform and Less Poverty in Brazil." The program is aimed at providing land for 15,000 poor families in the states of Pernambuco, Bahia, Ceara, Maranhao and Minas Gerais.
-- CVRD'S SALE TO HELP BRAZIL'S EXTERNAL ACCOUNTS

A financial institution that is part of one consortium interested in bidding at the privatization auction of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce has asked Brazil's Central Bank to directly convert $800 million to reais to buy a stake in the mining firm.
-- CANADA WANTS AGREEMENT WITH MERCOSUR

Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and Canadian Prime-Minister Jean Chretien announced the Canadian government and members of the Mercosur trade bloc plan talks on a free trade agreement in parallel with negotiations for the Free Trade Area of the Americas.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- PERUVIAN ARMY FREES HOSTAGES
Peruvian troops stormed the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima and released 71 hostages kept for 126 days by Marxist rebels.
-- YOUTH ADMITS GROUP PLANNED ATTACK TO INDIAN
The five youths that burned a Brazilian indian prepared the attack for nearly two hours, according to a testimony by one of the youths involved to the Police.
O GLOBO
-- JUDGE SAYS SON SHOULD PAY FOR INDIAN'S DEATH
Judge Novely Villanova da Silva Reis, father of one of the five youths that burned and killed a Brazilian indian over the weekend, said his son should pay for what he has done.
-- SUPREME COURT GRANTS INJUNCTION AGAINST CVRD'S AUCTION

Justice Marco Aurelio Mello granted an injunction suspending the transfer of 411,000 hectares near the Carajas iron mine to state mining firm Companhia Vale do Rio Doce and suggested the National Development Bank should delay CVRD's privatization auction.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
